answer: The BCG × prior-medical-history interaction on COVID-19 severity is not statistically significant. In the primary proportional-odds ordinal logistic model (N=153 subjects with a COVID-19–related AE; outcome = max AESEV 1–4; controlling for patients_seen), the interaction odds ratio is OR = 0.74 (95% CI 0.20–2.80, Wald p = 0.66). The point estimate (<1) suggests BCG vaccination attenuates the increase in COVID-19 severity odds associated with prior medical history (prior history main effect OR ≈ 2.1; BCG main effect OR ≈ 1.5), but the evidence is weak and imprecise. Sensitivity analyses agree that there is no reliable interaction: adding no-COVID subjects as a bottom level gives OR = 1.27 (95% CI 0.60–2.68, p = 0.54) — direction reverses — and replacing patients_seen with expect_interact gives OR = 0.66 (95% CI 0.18–2.48, p = 0.54). Bottom line: no detectable interaction; direction unstable across specifications.
